what: UPS delivers packages. It runs an integrated air and ground network in more than 200 countries, delivering around 20 million packages a day, and also offers freight, customs brokerage and contract logistics.
customers: Retailers and e-commerce sellers, manufacturers, healthcare companies and consumers.
money: ground and air delivery within the United States
freight forwarding, brokerage and healthcare logistics
moat: An integrated network of aircraft, hubs and drivers that took a century to build, and density that makes each additional stop cheaper.
risks: Revenue has been falling as it deliberately gives up low-margin Amazon volume
The Teamsters contract raised labour costs substantially
E-commerce shippers keep pushing for lower prices
The dividend payout is high relative to current earnings
opportunities: Shifting the mix toward healthcare logistics and small business raises revenue per package
Network closures and automation are cutting fixed costs
A dividend yield near 6% is supported if cash flow stabilises
watch: US average revenue per package and whether volume stabilises after the Amazon reduction.
